## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sūkaramukhapetavatthu* (Pv 2) is a canonical verse narrative located in the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Translated into English as *The Story of a Ghost With a Pig’s Mouth*, its central moral lesson is that even the use of harsh speech is enough to cause severe karmic retribution and suffering in the afterlife [SuttaCentral].
An early European translation from the Pali was published in French under the title *Histoire du Preta à museau de cochon (Sukara-mukha-peta-vatthu)* in the volume *Fragments extraits du Kandjour* (1883) [Fragments extraits du Kandjour 1883]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations across five languages [SuttaCentral].
Regarding text reuse and parallels, SuttaCentral lists no parallels for this text [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies five Pali-internal matches between Pv 2 and its commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, with the longest shared passage occurring across segments 3.1–3.4 (aligned with commentary segments 68–69); no cross-language matches above threshold are detected [DharmaNexus].
